cards.question: What is a CSS selector and what types exist?
cards.answer: A selector is a pattern for selecting HTML elements. Types: element (p), class (.class), ID (#id), attribute ([type]), combinators (div > p, div p, p + span, p ~ span), pseudo-class (:hover, :active, :first-child), pseudo-element (::before, ::after).
keyPoints: A pattern for selecting HTML elements for styling
Combinators: descendant (A B), child (A > B), adjacent (A + B), general (A ~ B)

cards.question: What is CSS selector specificity?
cards.answer: Specificity determines rule priority in conflicts. Calculated as a tuple (inline, ID, class, element): inline style > ID > class/attribute/pseudo-class > element/pseudo-element. NOT a decimal system: 11 classes don't outweigh 1 ID. !important overrides all specificity. At equal specificity, the last rule wins (cascade).
keyPoints: Tuple (inline, ID, class, element) — NOT a decimal score system
11 classes do NOT outweigh 1 ID (common misconception)
At equal specificity, last rule in source wins (cascade)

cards.question: How does Flexbox work and what are its main properties?
cards.answer: Flexbox aligns elements in a one-dimensional row or column. Container: display: flex, flex-direction, justify-content (along axis), align-items (across). Elements: flex (grow/shrink/basis), align-self. gap — spacing. Perfect for navigation, cards, alignment.
keyPoints: Container: display: flex, flex-direction, justify-content, align-items

cards.question: What is the difference between justify-content and align-items?
cards.answer: justify-content aligns along the main axis (usually horizontal). align-items aligns along the cross axis (usually vertical). With flex-direction: column, axes swap. flex-start, center, space-between, space-around, etc. — values for both.
keyPoints: Values: flex-start, center, space-between, space-around, stretch

cards.question: How does CSS Grid work?
cards.answer: Grid aligns elements in a 2D table (rows AND columns). display: grid, grid-template-columns, grid-template-rows. Elements: grid-column, grid-row. Automatic layout. More powerful than Flexbox for complex layouts. vs Flexbox: Grid for 2D, Flexbox for 1D.
keyPoints: Grid for 2D layouts, Flexbox for 1D alignment

cards.question: How do you use media queries for responsive design?
cards.answer: @media (max-width: 768px) { } — for screens smaller than 768px. @media (min-width: 1024px) { } — for larger than 1024px. @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { } — for dark theme. Mobile-first: start with mobile styles, expand via min-width. Desktop-first uses max-width.
keyPoints: Mobile-first: base styles for mobile, expand via min-width

cards.question: What is transition in CSS?
cards.answer: transition smoothly changes a property. transition: background 0.3s ease; Background color changes over 0.3s with ease timing. Can use on all properties: transition: all 0.3s; Used on :hover, :focus. Best for simple transitions.
keyPoints: Smooth change of a CSS property between two states
Syntax: transition: property duration timing-function delay
Triggered when property changes (hover, focus, class toggle)
For simple transitions, @keyframes for complex animations

cards.question: How do you create a CSS animation with @keyframes?
cards.answer: @keyframes slidein { from { transform: translateX(-100%); } to { transform: translateX(0); } } .item { animation: slidein 0.5s ease-out; } More complex than transition. Can specify multiple steps (0%, 50%, 100%). animation-delay for delay.
keyPoints: animation: name duration timing-function on element

cards.question: What transformations can be applied to an element?
cards.answer: transform: rotate(45deg), scale(1.5), translateX(50px), skew(10deg), perspective(1000px). Can combine: transform: rotate(45deg) scale(1.5). Don't affect other elements (don't change flow). Efficient for animations (GPU acceleration).
keyPoints: rotate, scale, translate, skew — main transformations
Can combine in one transform property
Don't affect layout of other elements (don't change document flow)
Use GPU acceleration — efficient for animations

cards.question: What is SASS/SCSS and its advantages?
cards.answer: SASS is a CSS preprocessor with variables, nesting, mixins, functions. $color: red; .button { background: $color; } Nesting: .button { &:hover { } }. Better code organization. Compiles to regular CSS. Alternatives: PostCSS, Styled-components, CSS Modules.
keyPoints: CSS preprocessor with variables ($var), nesting, mixins
